title: Vaineau, Barachant & Andreev 2013 — Brain Invaders Adaptive versus Non-Adaptive P300 Brain-Computer Interface dataset (BI2013a)
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic recordings from 24 healthy subjects performing a visual P300 brain-computer interface task based on the Brain Invaders video game. The study compares adaptive versus non-adaptive calibration approaches using Riemannian geometry for classifier training. EEG data were acquired using 16 electrodes at 512 Hz sampling rate during sessions conducted at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, France in 2013.
methods_description: EEG recordings were acquired using 16 wet Silver/Silver Chloride electrodes (standard 10-20 montage) with a g.USBamp amplifier (g.tec) at 512 Hz sampling rate. Reference electrode was placed at left earlobe with ground at FZ. Subjects completed 8 sessions with 2 runs each (adaptive and non-adaptive, randomized order). Each run consisted of training (80 target and 400 non-target flashes) and online phases. Visual stimuli were presented as flashes of 36 symbols arranged in 12 groups on a ViewSonic 22-inch screen at 75-115 cm distance. Online feedback was provided through the Brain Invaders video game interface.
